answers.H1: The corrected target is a sufficient probe plan or an indistinguishable model set demonstrating that no permitted plan can meet the regret tolerance. A certificate must connect indistinguishability to the absence of a common acceptable action; use a pair when sufficient. A pair alone can fail because three models can have pairwise overlapping acceptable-action sets with an empty three-way intersection. In the source’s deterministic loss-table example, every pair shares a zero-loss action, but every action has worst-case regret 1 across all three. If permitted probes return identical responses, no plan can certify regret below 1. Source: [decision-certificate-correction.md](decision-certificate-correction.md).
answers.H2: Next research action: construct the finite model–calibration family while retaining the distinction between pair witnesses and larger indistinguishable sets; check whether each candidate set has a common action meeting the declared regret tolerance. This is proposed work, not completed research. Source: [decision-certificate-correction.md](decision-certificate-correction.md).
